overview.description: T4 DNA ligase glues DNA back together. Its buffer is the most thermosensitive reagent in the whole guide - 1-2 freeze/thaw cycles and it's done, so aliquot into 10 ul tubes. Controls aren't optional: they're your bumpers for debugging perishable reagents.
objectives: set up a T4 DNA ligase reaction
protect thermosensitive ligase buffer with tiny aliquots
design the full panel of control plates

steps.description: T4 DNA ligase glues DNA back together. Its buffer is the most thermosensitive reagent in the whole guide - 1-2 freeze/thaw cycles and it's done, so aliquot into 10 ul tubes. Controls aren't optional: they're your bumpers for debugging perishable reagents.
steps.intro: T4 DNA ligase glues DNA back together. Its buffer is the most thermosensitive reagent in the whole guide - 1-2 freeze/thaw cycles and it's done, so aliquot into 10 ul tubes. Controls aren't optional: they're your bumpers for debugging perishable reagents.

instructions.title: Aliquot the buffer
instructions.description: Split ligase buffer into 10 ul single-use tubes; only thaw one at a time.

instructions.title: Set up the reaction
instructions.description: Combine vector, insert, ligase and ATP-containing buffer at the right molar ratio; add kinase if ends are dephosphorylated.

instructions.title: Run the controls
instructions.description: Set up negative (no plasmid), positive (uncut), digest-only, ligation, and optional dephosphorylation plates.

instructions.title: Transform & interpret
instructions.description: Transform the ligation mix and read each control plate to localise any failure.

submission.description: Submit your ligation plus a labelled photo of all control plates, with a one-line interpretation of each.

kits.note: Join sticky/blunt ends; remember the 5'-phosphate and molar-ratio rules.

kits.note: Cut-and-paste a fragment into a vector end to end.
